title: What Mental Health Really Means
hook: Mental health isn't just the absence of illness — it's being able to cope with life's stresses, work, learn, and contribute. Everyone has it, and it can be cared for.
key_points: Mental health is a state of wellbeing, not merely the absence of a disorder.
It shapes how we handle stress, relate to others, and make choices.
It exists on a continuum and shifts over time, like physical health.
It's influenced by biology, life circumstances, and social conditions — not personal weakness.
content_html: We often only talk about mental health when something goes wrong. But the World Health Organization frames it more broadly: mental health is something everyone has, all the time, and it's worth understanding before a crisis.
extra_html: The WHO defines mental health as a state of wellbeing in which a person can cope with the normal stresses of life, realize their abilities, learn and work well, and contribute to their community. By that definition it's far more than the absence of a diagnosable disorder — and, like physical health, it sits on a continuum that shifts over a lifetime. The WHO emphasizes that mental health is shaped by a combination of individual factors (genetics, temperament, health), life circumstances, and social and economic conditions such as work, housing, and relationships. That matters because it reframes mental health struggles as something influenced by real, often external forces — not a sign of weakness — and as something that can be protected and supported, just like the rest of your health.

related.title: Recognizing Depression and Anxiety
related.hook: Depression and anxiety are among the most common — and most treatable — health conditions. Knowing the signs is the first step to getting help that works.

related.title: Building Everyday Resilience
related.hook: Resilience isn't a personality you're born with — it's a set of habits and connections you can build, the way you build a muscle.

flashcards.prompt: According to the WHO, mental health is best described as:

choices.text: A state of wellbeing, not just the absence of illness
Simply not having a diagnosed disorder
A fixed trait you're born with

flashcards.explanation_html: The WHO defines mental health as a state of wellbeing that lets people cope with stress, realize their abilities, learn, work, and contribute — more than the mere absence of a disorder.

flashcards.prompt: What shapes a person's mental health?
flashcards.back_html: A mix of biological, personal, and social factors — genetics, life circumstances, relationships, and conditions like poverty or stress — not personal weakness.
